title: Sero te amavi
byline: From the Confessions of St. Augustine

latin: pulchritudo tam antiqua et tam nova,
english: Too late loved I Thee, O Thou Beauty of ancient days,
yet ever new! too late I loved Thee!

latin: Et ecce intus eras et ego foris,
et in ista formosa quae fecisti
english: And behold, Thou wert within, and I abroad,
and there I searched for Thee; deformed I,
plunging amid those fair forms which Thou hadst made.

latin: Mecum eras, et tecum non eram.
Ea me tenebant longe a te,
quae si in te non essent, non essent.
english: Thou wert with me, but I was not with Thee.
Things held me far from Thee, which,
unless they were in Thee, were not at all.
Thou calledst, and shoutedst, and burstest my deafness.
Thou flashedst, shonest, and scatteredst my blindness.

latin: fragrasti, et duxi spiritum et anhelo tibi;
tetigisti me, et exarsi in pacem tuam.
english: Thou breathedst odours, and I drew in breath
and panted for Thee. I tasted, and hunger and thirst.
Thou touchedst me, and I burned for Thy peace.

latin: pulchritudo tam antiqua et tam nova,
english: Too late loved I Thee, O Thou Beauty of ancient days,
yet ever new! too late I loved Thee!
